issueContext.title: VolumeAttachment is not deleted when the CSI plugin change from requiring attach to not requiring attach
issueContext.body:
### What happened?

After [volumeAttacher.Attach](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/v1.32.0/pkg/volume/util/operationexecutor/operation_generator.go#L271) executes successfully, the volumeattachment will be created. At this point, if CSI's ATTACHREQUIRED changes from true to false, it will cause [MarkVolumeAsAttached](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/v1.32.0/pkg/volume/util/operationexecutor/operation_generator.go#L301) to fail.
 And the volume will be removed from the [dsw](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/v1.32.0/pkg/controller/volume/attachdetach/populator/desired_state_of_world_populator.go#L166), leaving the VolumeAttachment stranded without being properly cleaned up.

### What did you expect to happen?

volumeattachment can be cleaned up.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

1. Install xsky-nfs-csi (other CSI drivers should be able to reproduce this) and set attachRequired to true
2. Create PVC and pod using the CSI
3. Keep querying volumeattachment using 'kubectl get volumeattachment'. As soon as the volumeattachment appears, immediately uninstall the CSI driver, then reinstall it with attachRequired set to false
4. After waiting for some time, query volumeattachment again and find that the volumeattachment still hasn't been deleted

### Anything else we need to know?

[operation_generator.go](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/v1.32.0/pkg/volume/util/operationexecutor/operation_generator.go#L301-L307)
I think we should add error handling here to mark the volume as "Uncertain", so the volume can be added to asw, allowing the next retry to successfully remove the VolumeAttachment.
I have tested that this can solve the problem. If confirmed this is an issue, I will submit a PR

issueContext.title: client-go doesn't properly handle reloading trust anchors during cluster CA rotation
issueContext.body:
Discussed in SIG Auth: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1woLGRoONE3EBVx-wTb4pvp4CI7tmLZ6lS26VTbosLKM/edit#bookmark=id.5mfr9vowfkwr

The kube-apiserver serving root CA certificate is injected into pods at /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/ca.crt.

Client-go reads it once [here](https://github.com/kubernetes/client-go/blob/6c596fdbc11ce7779ee320c6a11df44c5d516d54/rest/config.go#L528).  Normally the transport is supposed to automatically reload the roots, but it doesn't set reloadTLSFiles if a CAFile is set [here](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/928adb27abf755b402be7594844e3c248b0b7670/staging/src/k8s.io/client-go/transport/transport.go#L155-L168).

The net effect is that most clients using InClusterConfig will find their connection to kube-apiserver permanently broken during a rotation of the kube-apiserver serving CA, and won't recover until they are restarted.

We should:
* Set reloadTLSFiles when CAFile is set.
* Make sure that reloadTLSFiles will actually re-read the CAFile.
* Add a test.

/sig auth

issueContext.title: PodAffinity's QHint misses the scenario with existing pods' anti-affinity
issueContext.body:
### What happened?

/sig scheduling

The inter-pod affinity plugin is filtering out the nodes that have running pods with pod-anti-affinity that hates the pod being scheduled.
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/849a82b727b1cc1e77b58149b3cacbfa5ada30fd/pkg/scheduler/framework/plugins/interpodaffinity/filtering.go#L427-L429

However PodAffinity's QHint only checks if a pending pod's anti-affinity hates a deleted pod, and doesn't check if a deleted pod's anti-affinity hates a pending pod.
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/849a82b727b1cc1e77b58149b3cacbfa5ada30fd/pkg/scheduler/framework/plugins/interpodaffinity/plugin.go#L202-L207 

It causes the inter-pod affinity plugin to miss the pod/delete events that could make pending pods schedulable.

### What did you expect to happen?

PodAffinity's QHint checks _both_ if a pending pod's anti-affinity hates a deleted pod _and_ if a deleted pod's anti-affinity hates a pending pod.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

.

### Anything else we need to know?

 

### Kubernetes version

issueContext.title: NodeResourcesBalancedAllocation does not "Favors nodes that would obtain a more balanced resource usage if the Pod is scheduled there"
issueContext.body:
### What would you like to be added?

The [doc](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/scheduling/config/#scheduling-plugins) says:

> `NodeResourcesBalancedAllocation`: Favors nodes that would obtain a more balanced resource usage if the Pod is scheduled there.

But reading at the code it:

> Favors nodes that would obtain the most balanced resource usage once the Pod is scheduled there.

It would be good to have a plugin that scores according to how the balancing improves.

i.e.

instead of calculating score like this:

```math
S_1 = 100 - 100 * abs \left( \frac{\text{node memory requests} + \text{pod memory request}}{\text{node memory allocatable}} - \frac{\text{node cpu requests} + \text{pod cpu request}}{node cpu allocatable} \right) / 2
```

calculate the ratio improvement, by first calculating ratio before the pod is scheduled:

```math

S_2 = 100 - 100 * abs \left( \frac{\text{node memory requests}}{\text{node memory allocatable}} - \frac{\text{node cpu requests}}{node cpu allocatable} \right) / 2
```
And measuring the improvement

```math
S = max (0, S_1 - S_2)
```

Note: the formula here is incorrect and can be reduced, but you have the idea.

Bonus: Here is a prometheus query to calculate the score (NB: you need to add requested resources to have the exact value):

```
100
-
100
*
abs(
    (
        (
            sum(cluster:namespace:pod_memory:active:kube_pod_container_resource_requests)
            by (node)
            /
            sum(kube_node_status_allocatable{resource="memory"}) by (node)
        )

        -
        (
            sum(cluster:namespace:pod_cpu:active:kube_pod_container_resource_requests)
            by (node)
            /
            sum(kube_node_status_allocatable{resource="cpu"}) by (node)
        )
    )
    /
    2
)
```

### Why is this needed?

When scheduling a pod that is well balanced, the already well balanced nodes are favoured.

issueContext.body:
### What happened?

We observed the e2e test `External Storage [Driver: disk.csi.azure.com] [Testpattern: Dynamic PV (default fs)] read-write-once-pod [MinimumKubeletVersion:1.27] should preempt lower priority pods using ReadWriteOncePod volumes` causes flakes in other e2e tests in a downstream CI job with Azure Disk CSI driver.

[The test](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/4e94e70dcad423e9f59f12ac5a048d2137d20e86/test/e2e/storage/testsuites/readwriteoncepod.go#L133) runs a default (low-prio) pod1 with a `ReadWriteOncePod` volume and then starts a high prio pod2 that tries to use the same volume. To run pod2, the scheduler has to evict pod1 to make the RWOP volume "free" for pod2. That works great, however, it may evict also pods of other e2e tests that run with the default priority.

What happened on a busy clusters, with all nodes at their attachment limit.

1. pod1 runs, pod2 is created.
2. The scheduler evicts pod1. That frees the RWOP volume and it also frees the last attachment slot on the node.
3. Some other e2e tests creates a Pod and scheduler puts it on the node, taking the last attachment slot.
4. The scheduler schedules pod2 agaian and it sees there is no node with a free attachment slot -> new round of eviction, now evicting a pod of unrelated e2e tests. The unrelated test will fail.  

We observed it with Azure, which can attach only 8 disks on the cheaper nodes, so it's more reproducible there.

The preemption test should not affect other e2e tests

We observed an IPVS cleanup failure in Kubernetes v1.34.0.

issueContext.title: scheduler_unschedulable_pods metric might broke when running PreEnqueue plugins
issueContext.body:
### What happened?

`scheduler_unschedulable_pods` metric stores the number of unschedulable pods broken down by plugin name. It is incremented when the pod is re-added to the scheduling queue (with its all unschedulable and pending plugins) as well as when `PreEnqueue` plugin fails for such pod. When the pod is popped out from the scheduling queue, the metric is decremented using pod's unschedulable and pending pods lists. However, if `PreEnqueue` fails for a plugin that was already reported as unschedulable for a pod, the metric is still incremented (multiple ones for one plugin and one pod) what leads to not clearing the metric properly when popping out the pod.

### What did you expect to happen?

`scheduler_unschedulable_pods` metric to be incremented properly when `PreEnqueue` fails.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Create a pod that will get rejected by a plugin while scheduling (e.g. on `Filter`) and then blocked by `PreEnqueue` by the same plugin. If the pod is finally scheduled, the `scheduler_unschedulable_pods` will be non-zero.

Currently, some components in Kubernetes have been migrated (or partially migrated) to [contextual logging](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/blob/master/keps/sig-instrumentation/3077-contextual-logging/README.md). issueContext.body:
### What happened?

When a Service has zero backing Pods (e.g., Deployment scaled to 0 or no Pods ever matched the selector), the EndpointSlice object returned by the API server contains:
```
{
  "kind": "EndpointSliceList",
  "apiVersion": "discovery.k8s.io/v1",
  "metadata": {
    "resourceVersion": "828044619"
  },
  "items": [
    {
      "metadata": { ... },
      "addressType": "IPv4",
      "endpoints": null,  // null here
      "ports": null
    }
  ]
}
```
This breaks clients / validators that rely on the published OpenAPI schema where `endpoints` is treated as a required field and modeled as an array (not nullable).

### What did you expect to happen?

According to the API Spec, `endpoints` should be a JSON array. For the “no endpoints” case, it should be an empty array.

When creating a Service with ipFamilyPolicy: RequireDualStack or PreferredDualstack on Windows nodes, kube-proxy sometimes programs incorrect load balancers.

The issue manifests in two main ways:

1. Incorrect backend selection
    - IPv6 endpoints are sometimes programmed as backends for IPv4 VIPs
    - IPv4 endpoints are sometimes programmed as backends for IPv6 VIPs
    - This results in traffic blackholing or connection failures

2. Incorrect load balancer flags

   - IPv4 flags are sometimes applied to IPv6 load balancers

These issues appear intermittent and are more frequently observed under:

- Endpoint updates
- Service updates
- Rapid pod churn

For a RequireDualStack Service:

- IPv4 VIPs should:
    - Use only IPv4 endpoints
    - Be programmed with IPv4-specific HNS flags

- IPv6 VIPs should:
    - Use only IPv6 endpoints
    - Be programmed with IPv6-specific HNS flags

issueContext.title: Memleak in client-go transport.tlsCache
issueContext.body:
### What happened?

We're using a long-running process that connects to thousands of kubernetes cluster via client-go (not all simultaneously).
We noticed that the more kubernetes clusters we connect to and the longer the process runs, the more memory our process consumes over time.
An analysis with pprof confirmed that it looks like a memory leak in transport.tlsCache.

### What did you expect to happen?

Memory to be freed of clients that aren't used anymore, especially when the client object is not referenced anymore.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Connect to different k8s clusters with cert-base auth in a long-running process and watch memory usage grow.

### Anything else we need to know?

Reason for the leak:
We're using `kubernetes.NewForConfig` which eventually calls `transport.New(config)`
That transport calls `tlsCache.get`: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/3b5044fefd5a9a192b379236fac11ac8c41a7017/staging/src/k8s.io/client-go/transport/transport.go#L50

`tlsCache` is a non-exported global that implements a http transport cache. The `get` also stores the given transport in the cache if it's not there, yet.
However there are no mechanisms that would remove something from the cache. Neither explicitly, nor through expiration or anything.
The cache key includes k8s cert data which means every cluster we connect to will create a new cache entry that will then stay there indefinitely.

issueContext.body:
### What happened?

Hello,

I've been debugging issues with my Kubernetes nodes having very high CPU usage in network components.

I've finally traced down the origin to that block of code, which is overriding sysctl settings for iptables with insanely high values.
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/proxy/conntrack/sysctls.go#L62

The default is for the kernel to configurable iptables data structures based on available memory. Typically 32k-256k buckets and 256k max entries (this may be a tad low for the most busy servers).

issueContext.title: Kubelet sets incorrect ownerReference apiVersion "core/v1" on PodCertificateRequest, breaking garbage collection
issueContext.body:
### What happened?

When the kubelet creates a `PodCertificateRequest` (KEP-4317, `certificates.k8s.io/v1alpha1`), it sets the owning Pod's `ownerReference.apiVersion` to `"core/v1"` instead of the correct `"v1"`. This causes the GC controller in controller-manager to log errors like:

```
error syncing item" err="unable to get REST mapping for core/v1/Pod."
```

When a Pod is deleted, its associated `PodCertificateRequest` objects are never garbage collected.

### What did you expect to happen?

The `ownerReference` on `PodCertificateRequest` objects should use `apiVersion: "v1"` for Pod references, consistent with how all other core-group resources are referenced throughout Kubernetes. issueContext.title: kubelet TopologyManager Stalls on Large NUMA Systems (e.g. Nvidia GB200 Compute Tray with 34 NUMA nodes)
issueContext.body:
### What happened?

When scheduling a pod (e.g. KubeVirt virt-launcher pod) that requests a PCI device on a very large NUMA system, kubelet’s TopologyManager never finishes computing topology hints and the pod is effectively stuck in admission:

- The pod is scheduled to the node.
- kubelet never reaches the device Allocate call for the requested resource.
- From a higher-level consumer (KubeVirt in our case), the virt-launcher pod stays in Pending and the VM remains in Starting with Ready = False.
- kubelet is responsive, but many goroutines are stuck in topology hint generation.

In our environment this manifests as:

- KubeVirt VM with a hostDevice (GPU, InfiniBand or NVMe) never transitions to Running, even though the node has the capacity and the device is free.
- Disabling TopologyManager or constraining the NUMA fan-out immediately lets the VM start

### What did you expect to happen?

issueContext.body:
## Problem

The `appProtocol` field (GA since v1.20) is not displayed in `kubectl describe service` output, even when set. Users must use `kubectl get svc -o yaml` to verify this field.

This can be problematic when debugging Service Mesh or Gateway API configurations where `appProtocol` affects traffic routing. Given that `appProtocol` has been GA for several years and is actively used in Service Mesh environments, displaying it in `kubectl describe` output would be beneficial for users.

## Proposed Solution

Display `appProtocol` in the port section of `kubectl describe service` output:
```
Port:              http  80/TCP
TargetPort:        8080/TCP
AppProtocol:       http          # <-- Add this

issueContext.title: setcap build image shouldn't require a shell
issueContext.body:
### What would you like to be added?

Building with a more vanilla setcap image shouldn't require a shell in the image to run the command 


in `build/server-image/kube-apiserver/Dockerfile`

```sh
# We apply cap_net_bind_service so that kube-apiserver can be run as
# non-root and still listen on port less than 1024
RUN setcap cap_net_bind_service=+ep /${BINARY}
```

this command requires the `SETCAP_IMAGE` have a shell in order to:
1) RUN a command that isn't in the form of ["/usr/sbin/setcap", "..."] 
2) shell expand the `${BINARY}` argument


### Why is this needed?

By making this change you can eliminate the need of having a shell in the setcap image:


```diff
diff --git a/build/server-image/kube-apiserver/Dockerfile b/build/server-image/kube-apiserver/Dockerfile
index 27129d29bd9..acfe8c26f22 100644
--- a/build/server-image/kube-apiserver/Dockerfile
+++ b/build/server-image/kube-apiserver/Dockerfile
@@ -20,11 +20,11 @@ ARG SETCAP_IMAGE
 # to setup qemu for the builder.
 FROM --platform=linux/$BUILDARCH ${SETCAP_IMAGE}
 ARG BINARY
-COPY --chmod=755 ${BINARY} /${BINARY}
+COPY --chmod=755 ${BINARY} /set_cap_binary
 # We apply cap_net_bind_service so that kube-apiserver can be run as
 # non-root and still listen on port less than 1024
-RUN setcap cap_net_bind_service=+ep /${BINARY}
+RUN ["setcap", "cap_net_bind_service=+ep", "/set_cap_binary"]
 
 FROM --platform=linux/$TARGETARCH ${BASEIMAGE}
 ARG BINARY
-COPY --from=0 /${BINARY} /usr/local/bin/${BINARY}
+COPY --from=0 /set_cap_binary /usr/local/bin/${BINARY}
```

issueContext.title: Let DRA drivers specify the order in which devices are considered during scheduling
issueContext.body:
### What would you like to be added?

Currently the order in which the DRA allocator considers devices during scheduling is non-deterministic. Since the DRA allocator uses a first-fit algorithm, the order in which devices are considered can impact both the time required to schedule pods and which devices are selected.

We want to let DRA drivers specify the order in which the allocator will consider devices. This is discussed in more detail in https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/5773 and https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/pull/5794.

### Why is this needed?

This will allow faster scheduling and allocation of more appropriate devices.

issueContext.title: RFE: Kubectl wait for multiple conditions
issueContext.body:
**What would you like to be added**:
I'd like `kubectl wait` to support multiple wait conditions at once so these are evaluated on the resource with the same ResourceVersion. Like:
```
kubectl wait <resource> --for='condition=Available=True' --for='condition=Progressing=False' --for='condition=Degraded=False
```

**Why is this needed**:
The current workaround
```
kubectl wait <resource> --for='condition=Available=True' && \
kubectl wait <resource> --for='condition=Progressing=False' && \
kubectl wait <resource> --for='condition=Degraded=False'
```
isn't atomic and the first condition can change before it evaluates the next one. It's also slower and uses more calls to the apiserver.

/sig cli
fyi @soltysh

issueContext.body:
For the beta promotion of `DRADeviceBindingConditions` (DBC), we have listed below the metrics that are planned for implementation to bring this feature to a production-ready state.

1.  #### _The number of times and the status BindingConditions are processed during PreBind_
	Counts the number of scheduling attempts where at least one `ResourceClaim` is allocated to a device with `BindingConditions`. In addition, by specifying `success`, `failure`, or `timeout` with the label `status`, users can view the counts for each BindingConditions processing status. ### What would you like to be added?

### What would you like to be added?

Add an option to the [resourceslice controller](https://github.com/kubernetes/dynamic-resource-allocation/blob/master/resourceslice/resourceslicecontroller.go) (e.g. **`ReconcilePoolWithName`**) so that when it is set (e.g. to the node name):

- **Owner** remains Node (OwnerRef for GC when the node is removed).
- **Do not** set `ResourceSlice.Spec.NodeName` so the scheduler can use `NodeSelector` or `allNodes`.
- **Watch** all ResourceSlices for the driver (no `ResourceSliceSelectorNodeName` in list/watch), but in the informer **only enqueue work for slices whose `Spec.Pool.Name == ReconcilePoolWithName`**. Each node’s controller then reconciles only its own pool (e.g. pool name = node name).

}

### What happened?

In this [OpenShift CI run](https://prow.ci.openshift.org/view/gs/test-platform-results/logs/periodic-ci-openshift-multiarch-master-nightly-4.21-ocp-e2e-ovn-remote-s2s-libvirt-ppc64le/1999572809340162048), the upstream `[sig-node] Lifecycle sleep action zero value when create a pod with lifecycle hook using sleep action with a duration of zero seconds prestop hook using sleep action with zero duration` test failed because SyncTerminatedPod timed out. The kubelet logs shows:

```
Dec 12 21:19:08.719197 compute-1 kubenswrapper[7200]: E1212 21:19:08.719175    7200 pod_workers.go:1324] "Error syncing pod, skipping" err="failed to delete cgroup paths for [kubepods besteffort poda4418b44-5c5a-4bd5-b7b3-42860ff00483] : unable to destroy cgroup paths for cgroup [kubepods besteffort poda4418b44-5c5a-4bd5-b7b3-42860ff00483] : Timed out while waiting for systemd to remove kubepods-besteffort-poda4418b44_5c5a_4bd5_b7b3_42860ff00483.slice" pod="e2e-pod-lifecycle-sleep-action-allow-zero-761/pod-with-prestop-sleep-hook-zero-duration" podUID="a4418b44-5c5a-4bd5-b7b3-42860ff00483"
```

The systemd journal reveals that the slice was actually removed successfully ~30 seconds before the kubelet timeout:

Pod deletion should complete promptly after containers terminate, without a 30-second timeout.

2. Run a workload that creates and deletes many pods rapidly

issueContext.title: Support TLS Server Name overrides in EgressSelectorConfiguration
issueContext.body:
## What would you like to be added?

Add a `tlsServerName` field to the `TLSConfig` structure in `EgressSelectorConfiguration` to allow overriding the hostname used for TLS certificate verification, similar to the existing `tls-server-name` field in kubeconfig (added in[ #88769](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/88769)).

## Precedent

This functionality already exists in:
- **kubeconfig files**: The `tls-server-name` field was added in #88769 for similar use cases
- **kubectl**: The `--tls-server-name` flag provides command-line access
- **Go's `tls.Config`**: The underlying `ServerName` field supports this

The egress selector `TLSConfig` would benefit from the same capability for consistency.

## Why is this needed?

### Use Case

This addresses scenarios where components using EgressSelectorConfiguration connect through Kubernetes Service DNS names (e.g., proxy.svc.cluster.local) but that hostname is not included in the server certificate's Subject Alternative Names (SANs), which define which hostnames a certificate is valid for.

**Example scenario:**
- Egress selector is configured to connect to: `https://konnectivity-service.example.svc.cluster.local:8443`
- The proxy's TLS certificate contains SANs for: `proxy.example.com`
- Connection fails because `konnectivity-service.example.svc.cluster.local` is not in the certificate SANs

### Current Workaround Limitations

The current workaround of updating certificates to include all possible service DNS names has significant drawbacks:
- Requires certificate regeneration and rotation across many clusters
- Service names may vary across environments (dev, staging, prod)
- Certificate management becomes complex in multi-tenant environments
- May require coordination with external PKI infrastructure

- DRA drivers can use list-type fields (`bools`/`ints`/`strings`/`versions`) for device attributes in ResourceSlice. The number of attribute values, including scalars and lists, per single device is limited to 48.
- The `matchAttribute`/`distinctAttribute` constraints in ResourceClaim now work on both scalar and list attributes. The `matchAttribute` constraint matches when the intersection of all list values among candidate devices is non-empty. The `distinctAttribute` constraint (behind the `ConsumableCapacity` feature gate) matches when all list values among candidate devices are pairwise disjoint. Scalar values are implicitly treated as a singleton set.
- Added a new CEL function `.includes` that works on both scalar and list attributes to test inclusion (e.g., `device.attributes["dra.example.com"].model.includes("model-a")`), supporting migration when a DRA driver changes an attribute value type from scalar to list or vice versa.
apiChange.author: everpeace
apiChange.userFacingChange:
[Alpha] Introduce List Types for Attributes in DRA (KEP-5491). 

The `DRAListTypeAttributes` feature gate(false by default) can activate below enhancements.

For DRA drivers, it can enable list-type fields(`bools/ints/strings/versions`) for device attributes in `ResourceSlice`. Please remember that the number of attribute values, including scalars and lists, per single device is limited to 48. 

For DRA users, this feature enhances the semantics of `matchAttribute`/`distinctAttribute` constraint in `ResourceClaim` to work on both scalar and list attributes. The `matchAttribute` constraint now matches when the intersection (as a set) of all the list values among candidate devices is non-empty. The `distinctAttribute` constraint, which is behind the `ConsumableCapacity` feature gate, matches when all the list values (as a set) among candidate devices are pairwise disjoint. In both constraints, scalar values are implicitly treated as a singleton set. 

And, a new CEL function `.includes`　is introduced. The function can work on both scalar and list attributes to test inclusion(e.g., `device.attributes["dra.example.com"].model.includes("model-a")`). This can support smooth migration for CEL expression in DRA resources when a DRA driver changes the attribute value type from scalar to list, or vice versa.

issueContext.title: Pod-level memory.min not reconciled when MemoryQoS config changes
issueContext.body:
### What happened?

When MemoryQoS is enabled with `memoryReservationPolicy=HardReservation`, the kubelet sets `memory.min` on pod-level cgroups. If the operator later disables MemoryQoS or switches to `memoryReservationPolicy=None` and restarts kubelet, the pod-level `memory.min` retains its previous non-zero value for existing pods.

QoS-level cgroups (`kubepods-burstable.slice`) are correctly reset via the periodic `setMemoryQoS()` loop, but pod-level cgroups are not reconciled.


### What did you expect to happen?

Pod-level `memory.min` should be reset to 0 when MemoryQoS is disabled or `memoryReservationPolicy` changes to `None`.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

   1. Start kubelet with `--feature-gates=MemoryQoS=true` and `memoryReservationPolicy: HardReservation`
   2. Create a Burstable pod with `requests.memory: 128Mi`
   3. Verify pod cgroup has `memory.min=134217728`
   4. Change kubelet config to disable MemoryQoS or set `memoryReservationPolicy: None`, restart kubelet
   5. Observe pod cgroup still has `memory.min=134217728`


### Anything else we need to know?

 This also affects the container-level `memory.min` set in `generateLinuxContainerResources()`, which only runs at container creation time. However, container-level is less impactful since containers are typically recreated more frequently than kubelet config changes.

 ### Related

   - KEP-2570: Memory QoS with cgroups v2
   - https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/137584
   - https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/137637
